quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more time and distance to stop than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time to avoid hitting you.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Your tires do not grip wet, snowy, or icy roads as well as they grip dry roads. You should slow down on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: What is this bicyclist signaling?
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use hand and arm signals instead. When a bicyclist puts their left arm straight out, they are signaling a left turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign tells you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median on a highway. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams can reflect off the weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Never try to pass more than one vehicle at a time.
questions.explanation: Never pass more than one vehicle at a time. Only pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Drinking coffee, eating, or taking a shower will not speed up this process.

questions.question: You notice the driver ahead of you is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Know that the driver is not paying full attention to the road.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving by talking to passengers, looking for things, reading, or daydreaming. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space. A distracted driver is more likely to have an accident.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to a steep hill ahead. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid accidents.

questions.question: A "No stopping" sign means you may stop only:

options.text: To avoid conflict with other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid conflict with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to follow a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: You had a stressful incident at work. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
questions.explanation: Wait and calm down before driving. Driving while angry or upset is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard lights and get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic. This alerts other drivers that you have a problem.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Check for injuries and call 911 if needed. Report the crash to police if there are injuries, deaths, or property damage over $1,000 (or over $200 to government property like signs).

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop before reaching a school bus with flashing red lights. Stay stopped until the lights turn off. On a road with a center median, vehicles on the opposite side do not need to stop.

questions.question: Driver fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue makes you slower to react, judge speed and distance, and make decisions. You could fall asleep while driving and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells drivers to slow down at an intersection and be ready to stop. Let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane will end. Drivers in the right lane must move to the left lane.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions per mile. You need to focus fully on driving. Any other task can be dangerous and distract you.

questions.question: Orange signs are used in construction work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are usually orange and diamond-shaped. Some are rectangular. These signs are reflective so they show up better at night.

questions.question: When you see an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you disapprove by making gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and increase the distance between you. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them or make gestures.

questions.question: A truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right. You should:

options.text: Wait until they finish turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until they finish turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait until they finish their turn before you make yours.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving. You should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects how safely you drive. Know your limits and only drive if you can do so safely.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. You must stop if:
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagperson signals you to stop, or a train is close. Never race a train.
